RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT

This Lease is made on April 14, 2026 between Harborview Ridge Holdings LLC, 2400 Broadway, Suite 500, Brooklyn, New York 11217 (the "Landlord"), and Nadia Okonkwo (the "Tenant").

1. PREMISES. The Landlord leases to the Tenant Apartment 4C at 88 Sterling Place, Brooklyn, New York 11217 (the "Premises"), for residential use only.

2. TERM. The term is one year, beginning May 1, 2026 and ending April 30, 2027.

3. RENT. The rent is $3,200 per month, payable in advance on the first day of each month. The Landlord will provide a written receipt for any rent paid other than by personal check. Rent is not considered late until five days after it is due, and the Landlord will send a written notice by certified mail if rent is not received within five days of the due date, as Real Property Law § 235-e requires.

4. LATE FEE. A late fee of the lesser of $50 or 5% of the monthly rent may be charged if rent is more than five days late.

5. SECURITY DEPOSIT. The Tenant will pay a security deposit of $3,200, which is one month's rent and is the maximum permitted by General Obligations Law § 7-108. The deposit is held in a segregated account at Peninsula Trust Bank, and the Landlord will notify the Tenant in writing of the bank's name and address. Within fourteen days after the Tenant vacates, the Landlord will return the deposit together with an itemized statement of any deductions. Failure to provide the statement within fourteen days forfeits the Landlord's right to retain any part of the deposit.

6. INSPECTION. The Tenant may request an inspection before the term begins and before vacating. The Landlord will give at least forty-eight hours' written notice of the inspection and will provide an itemized statement of proposed repairs.

7. WARRANTY OF HABITABILITY. The Premises are subject to the warranty of habitability under Real Property Law § 235-b, which cannot be waived. Any provision of this Lease purporting to waive it is void.

8. LANDLORD ACCESS. The Landlord may enter the Premises at reasonable times on reasonable prior notice for inspection, repairs, or to show the Premises, and without notice in an emergency.

9. RENEWAL AND TERMINATION. If the Landlord does not intend to renew this Lease or intends to raise the rent by more than five percent, the Landlord will give written notice of at least thirty days if the Tenant has occupied the Premises less than one year, sixty days if one to two years, and ninety days if more than two years, as Real Property Law § 226-c requires.

10. SUBLETTING. The Tenant may sublet with the Landlord's consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld, subject to Real Property Law § 226-b.

11. UTILITIES. The Tenant pays for electricity and gas. The Landlord pays for water, sewer, and heat.

12. SMOKE AND CARBON MONOXIDE DETECTORS. The Landlord has installed working smoke and carbon monoxide detectors. The Tenant will test them and notify the Landlord of any defect.

13. WINDOW GUARDS. WINDOW GUARDS ARE REQUIRED IF A CHILD TEN YEARS OF AGE OR YOUNGER RESIDES IN THE PREMISES. The Tenant has completed the annual window-guard notice attached as Exhibit A.

14. LEAD PAINT. The building was constructed before 1978. The Tenant acknowledges receipt of the federal lead-hazard pamphlet and the disclosure attached as Exhibit B.

15. BEDBUG DISCLOSURE. The Landlord has provided the bedbug infestation history for the building and the Premises as Administrative Code § 27-2018.1 requires, attached as Exhibit C.

16. ATTORNEYS' FEES. If either party brings an action to enforce this Lease, the prevailing party is entitled to reasonable attorneys' fees, as Real Property Law § 234 provides reciprocally.

17. GOVERNING LAW. New York law governs this Lease.

LANDLORD                                  TENANT
